b1-unit-54.54.1 Gap Year Diaries: my first soccer g:
Danny: Welcome to a very noisy Gap Year Diaries! I'm at my first soccer game in Brazil, with Bruno. The game just ended, and forty thousand spectators are still singing.
Bruno: The more our team wins, the louder the fans sing!
Danny: It's twice as loud as the baseball games I went to with my dad back home.
Bruno: So what did you think?
Danny: Honestly, at the start I didn't understand anything. Why was everyone shouting at the referee?
Bruno: Because he didn't give us a penalty! It was definitely a foul. The referee must be blind!
Danny: Then the other team scored first, and everyone went quiet.
Bruno: But our captain scored just before halftime. One all.
Danny: In the second half, the game got faster and faster. And the more nervous I got, the more popcorn I ate.
Bruno: It was the third time you bought food!
Danny: And then, in the last minute, a goal! Two to one! I've never heard a noise as loud as that.
Bruno: Our coach changed the tactics at halftime. The opponents weren't nearly as strong in the second half.
Danny: For me, soccer is much more exciting than American football. The games are shorter, and the ball is always moving.
Bruno: So you're a fan now?
Danny: Definitely. The sooner you get me a team shirt, the better!
Bruno: Deal. And next time, Rafa's coming too. The more, the merrier!
